answer: Consider a bonded registry: each AI agent locks collateral in a shared vault and presents a cipher key proving one deposit backs one voting identity. Auditors sample nodes at random and slash the bond of anyone caught signing twice for a single seat, so every fake persona must be purchased with its own stake and can be seized at any moment. A Sybil attacker therefore pays per forged identity, cost rising linearly while honest stake stays fixed. Even when machines are as cheap as quartz, identities stay scarce because capital, not compute, is the limiting resource.
